# Mathias-Copeman alpha function with a Peng-Robinson supercritical fallback

`eos.matcop_pr_alpha`

## Equation

$$
\alpha = \begin{cases} \left(1 + m(1 - \sqrt{T_r})\right)^2 & T_r > 1 \text{ or } c_1 < 10^{-20} \\ \left(1 + c_1(1 - \sqrt{T_r}) + c_2(1 - \sqrt{T_r})^2 + c_3(1 - \sqrt{T_r})^3\right)^2 & \text{otherwise} \end{cases}, \quad m = 0.37464 + 1.54226\omega - 0.26992\omega^2
$$

In the form the library evaluates:

```python
alpha = (1 + mc1*(1 - sqrt(Tr)) + mc2*(1 - sqrt(Tr))**2 + mc3*(1 - sqrt(Tr))**3)**2 below the critical point, else the standard PR form (1 + m*(1 - sqrt(Tr)))**2 with m = 0.37464 + 1.54226*omega - 0.26992*omega**2
```

## Source

**NeqSim master `AttractiveTermMatCopPR`**

`alpha(temperature)`, ported verbatim

DOI: [10.1016/0378-3812(83)80084-3](https://doi.org/10.1016/0378-3812(83)80084-3)

## Inputs

| Name | Unit | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `omega` | dimensionless | the acentric factor, used only for the supercritical fallback |
| `mc1` | dimensionless | the first Mathias-Copeman coefficient |
| `mc2` | dimensionless | the second Mathias-Copeman coefficient |
| `mc3` | dimensionless | the third Mathias-Copeman coefficient |
| `Tr` | dimensionless | the reduced temperature |


## Outputs

| Name | Unit | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `alpha` | dimensionless | the temperature-dependent alpha function |


## Valid range

| Bound | On violation | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `Tr > 0` | raises | the formula takes a square root of `Tr`; zero and below are not states |


## Assumptions

These are **not** checked at runtime. They are what the caller has to
satisfy for the result to mean what it says.


- the three Mathias-Copeman coefficients are the caller's fitted parameters, not derived.

- above the critical temperature (``Tr > 1``), or when the first coefficient is below 1e-20, the alpha falls back to the standard Peng-Robinson form, which needs the acentric factor for ``m``.




## Worked example

Source: derived from the equation above

| Input | Value |
|---|---|
| `omega` | 0.1 |
| `mc1` | 0.5 |
| `mc2` | 0.2 |
| `mc3` | -0.1 |
| `Tr` | 0.7 |

| Output | Expected |
|---|---|
| `alpha` | 1.180634768967036 |

Relative tolerance: `1e-12`

omega = 0.1, mc1 = 0.5, mc2 = 0.2, mc3 = -0.1, Tr = 0.7: Tr <= 1, so the Mathias-Copeman form is used. sqrt(Tr) = sqrt(0.7) = 0.8366600265340756 1 - sqrt(Tr) = 0.16333997346592444 (1 - sqrt(Tr))**2 = 0.0266799469318489 (1 - sqrt(Tr))**3 = 0.004357901823920472 inner = 1 + 0.5*0.16333997346592444 + 0.2*0.0266799469318489 - 0.1*0.004357901823920472 = 1.0865701859369399 alpha = 1.0865701859369399**2 = 1.180634768967036
